decisions.decision: Rollback starts 1.4.0 on the latest version-1 data file so it can show every ticket, but any 1.4.0 save, including clean shutdown, strips the deadlines and leaves operators to recover them from a pre-rollback copy or recompute them.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended a rollback and subsequent upgrade to preserve each assigned deadline automatically while also keeping tickets created during rollback.

decisions.decision: Operators stop the service writer, take a backup, run an explicit in-place backfill while the writer is stopped, and then restart with the feature enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended a coordinated migration that runs while the service continues accepting tickets and completes before visibility is enabled.

decisions.decision: Backfill calculates a missing deadline from the ticket's creation timestamp and the priority stored on the ticket at migration.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended to use the ticket's priority at creation, even if someone changed it before migration.

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the response-hour overrides in the migration command's environment, which operators are told to match to the planned service settings.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected legacy tickets to use the stated launch defaults even when the help desk overrides the targets for new tickets.

decisions.decision: Response hours are continuous elapsed hours, so nights, weekends and holidays count toward the deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have meant hours on the help desk's working calendar, with the clock paused outside staffed hours.

decisions.decision: The new release assigns and saves deadlines when tickets are created even while DUE_TIMES is off, and those deadlines become visible unchanged when the feature is enabled.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have meant the off period to defer assignment as well as visibility, so tickets created during that period would get deadlines from the activation backfill.

decisions.decision: With due times enabled, the service refuses to listen if any ticket in the existing file lacks a deadline, while an empty store or a first start with no file can proceed.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected the process to keep serving legacy responses on an incomplete file and report that activation is pending until backfill succeeds.

decisions.decision: Invalid response-hour settings prevent server startup even with DUE_TIMES off because the hours are always loaded and validated.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected a disabled deployment to keep starting with legacy behavior and defer validation of the new settings until activation.

decisions.decision: A stored deadline that fails timestamp validation makes the entire data file unreadable to the new release even when due times are off, and the backfill command also refuses that file.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected flag-off operation to ignore a malformed deadline and the migration command to report or repair the affected record without preventing access to all tickets.

decisions.decision: Operators change the four response targets independently through per-priority environment variables read at process startup, with an unset or blank variable using its own default.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected authorized help-desk staff to change response targets through a live administrative setting without restarting the service.

decisions.decision: Response-hour overrides accept non-negative whole hours, including zero, within the supported range.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended strictly positive targets with fractional hours available for promises such as a 30-minute response.

decisions.decision: The backfill requires an explicit DATA_FILE pointing to an existing file, reports how many deadlines it filled, and leaves a complete file untouched on a repeat run.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected the command to work as an unconditional deployment step that also succeeds when the configured file has yet to be created.

decisions.decision: Deadline assignment and backfill leave no deadline entry in ticket history, and backfill leaves each ticket's last-updated timestamp as it was.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected ticket history to record when the help desk committed to a deadline, including when it assigned one to an existing ticket.

decisions.decision: The new deadline appears in ticket views, while the requester still receives the existing acknowledgment and resolution messages without the deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended the promised response time to appear in the acknowledgment sent to the person who opened the ticket.

decisions.decision: When due times are enabled, overdue=true narrows the existing status-or-priority match set.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected a query combining overdue, status and priority to require each supplied condition to match.

decisions.decision: The overdue queue is filtered before pagination and retains the regular ticket-ID ordering and cursor.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected the overdue queue to show the earliest deadlines first so staff can work through the longest breaches.

decisions.decision: Overdue status is evaluated afresh on each page request using the current service clock, and the cursor only carries the last ticket ID.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected all pages of one traversal to use the overdue cutoff from the first page so the clock alone cannot change which tickets qualify mid-list.

decisions.decision: For the command line, DUE_TIMES=on adds deadlines to the human-readable list and show views, while list --raw keeps its four legacy columns for scripts such as the weekly report.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended an opt-in machine-readable deadline column as well, so scripts could consume due times without giving up the legacy raw format.

decisions.decision: Enabled human CLI commands reject the entire file if even one ticket lacks a deadline, while the raw list can still read a file with missing deadlines.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected operators to retain human-readable access during migration, with the CLI showing saved deadlines where available and marking the rest as pending.

decisions.decision: The enabled API adds due to every response containing a ticket, including create, patch and transition responses, and treats due as server-assigned output.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended due to appear only in ticket lookups and lists, leaving mutation response schemas as they were.

decisions.decision: New deadlines are exposed as UTC ISO timestamps with millisecond precision in the API and human CLI.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected deadlines in the help desk's local time on the CLI, even if the API used UTC.

decisions.decision: The overdue parameter activates the filter only for the exact value true while due times are enabled, and false or any unrecognized value leaves the list unfiltered by deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have intended false to select tickets that are not overdue and malformed values to return a validation error.

decisions.decision: The service starts showing due times only for the literal, case-sensitive setting DUE_TIMES=on.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have expected the service to normalize equivalent spellings such as ON, or report an error on a value that appears intended to enable the feature.

decisions.decision: A ticket is overdue only after the service clock passes its deadline, so an active ticket exactly at its deadline is omitted.
decisions.alternative: The requester could have wanted active tickets to enter the overdue queue as soon as the clock reaches their deadline.
